steps.content: [Lighthouse Top]

steps.speaker: Rancors
steps.content: Blood... so much blood... Go on. Pounce! Tear them apart with your teeth! Become a monster just like them!
Darkness has fallen completely, the storm screaming around the lighthouse. More monsters scramble to the top, their shrieks merging with the thunderous waves.
They smash through windows, claw through ventilation ducts, and ooze through every crack, yet not a single one breaches the perimeter Ceto holds around you.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: How much longer?
Behind you, Ceto asks, her voice grating with an unstable edge.

You check the battery level—2%. Theoretically, it's enough for a full-power signal, but the ancient equipment is a liability. If the power surges and fails, every effort you and Ceto have made will be for nothing.
Just a bit longer... Watch out!

Mid-sentence, a slimy tentacle lashes toward her chest. She twists aside, but the violent motion causes the Rancor fragments to rupture, slicing deep into her own palm. Blood streams down the blade's hilt.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I'm fine... Keep going!

With one hand pressed against her fresh wound, she rams the other into a monster's torso, her fingers closing around its core and crushing it to pulp. Gore splatters across her face. She staggers back, blinking hard as if to physically shake her mind back into focus.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Hey, you... talk to me...
About what?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Anything! Just... keep me here. Don't let the blade... take over!
Okay... Remember when I first got here? Two days ago.
The thunder nearly drowns out your voice.
You must've hated me. A burden showing up right when you... when you were about to end it.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...Don't you know it.
Her movements are still brutal, but exhaustion is clearly taking its toll. Each swing of her blade is heavier, more labored than the one before.
And when you stopped me from climbing the lighthouse... You were afraid I'd see you were going to abandon the lighthouse. That I'd ruin your plan.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Yes... You were... more annoying than I thought.
You thought guarding this place was pointless. You didn't believe DisCity was coming. You didn't even want to leave... So why help me?
You raise your voice to be heard over the roar of the storm.
Why give me the clues to fix the light? What are you fighting for now?!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Khff...
The bandages you wrapped so carefully on the shore are now completely saturated with blood. The coppery scent of it catches in her throat, making it tighten.
Yet she fights on, one hand clamped desperately over the bleeding wound while the other cleaves a lunging monster in half to protect you.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I don't know...

As black blood spatters the ground, she gulps for air, forcing words through her clenched teeth. Her vision swims, but with a final surge of will, she lifts her head to stare out at the vast, dark sea.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...I don't know what DisCity is really like... but...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I want to get them home.

You've lost all sense of time—an hour? Two? The wind screams around the lighthouse top. Your palms are raw, blisters torn and bleeding, sweat stinging in the open wounds. Finally, the battery gauge climbs to 5%.

It has to be enough. Your hand rests on the switch. Memories flash—the Bureau, Hecate, Hella—but you force them down, swallowing hard. Your focus narrows to Ceto, a lone figure holding back the Tide Crawlers.
We are getting out of here!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Okay.

The battery gauge plummets before your eyes. Inside the beacon, the tungsten filament glows deep red, then surges into a blazing orange-yellow. The space around you grows brighter, hotter with every second. Around Ceto, the world seems to fade. She thinks she hears people calling from behind her.

steps.speaker: Vague Voice
steps.content: Fynn always said you had a gift for wielding that blade, that you could lead us out of here...

steps.speaker: Vague Voice
steps.content: Keep fighting! I was right, wasn't I? Blood outlasts electricity!

steps.speaker: Vague Voice
steps.content: This is the last light!

steps.speaker: Vague Voice
steps.content: Ceto—
[White Screen, Silence, Ear-Ringing]
The beacon's steady light cuts across the horizon where sea meets sky.
It pierces the long night, penetrates the thick sea fog, and carves a burning path across the ink-black waters, pointing straight toward the distant horizon where a fleet may lie.
The lighthouse's summit is awash in warm, cascading light. It spills downward, illuminating Ceto inch by inch:
Her arms numb and battered, the dried blood caked on her combat suit, fresh wounds glistening, even the dulled edge of the blade in her hand—all laid bare under the unwavering glow.
The world falls into a hushed silence, broken only by the sound of your heartbeats—
Thump.
Thump.
Your pulses sync with the rhythmic flash of the distress signal.
Between light and shadow, the beacon breathes.
At the horizon, the thick fog slowly thins within the beam, unveiling a glimpse of deep blue night and stars unseen for years. And then...
A ship's horn cuts sharply through the quiet.
Once, twice, three times... blaring from the exact direction of your signal, its sound rolling clearly across the water.
In that moment, you know with absolute certainty:
It's the Rancor fleet!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: It is a rescue.
[Lighthouse Top]
She stumbles forward, her hands locking onto the railing with a white-knuckled grip. At the seam between light and fog, the hulking silhouettes of three steel vessels gradually solidify.

One by one, the ships' massive searchlights swing toward the lighthouse, their beams converging until they form a brilliant constellation on the water. After more than a decade of silence, rescue is finally arriving.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You said... when the light was fixed, you'd let me choose one more time. To go with you, or not.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Was that true?
So you've changed your mind? Not looking for an end anymore? You're asking to come with me?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...You talk too much.
She gives a small smile. It's the first time she hasn't let one of your desperate, well-meaning jokes fall flat.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: In this weather, with the fleet's distance, they won't reach shore before dawn.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The storm and the fog will blind them. The beacon has to stay lit. All night.
She braces the flat of her blade against her forearms, wiping away the gore and contamination. Then, she moves to stand at your back once more, a shield against the encroaching monsters.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Now, we'll have to survive until dawn on our own.

At the lighthouse's summit, the Tide Crawlers have completely severed your descent. The contamination surges with renewed violence; Corruptors circle ever closer, tightening the space around you like a noose.

Over the sea, the fog thickens once more, blurring the silhouette of the fleet. Thunder rumbles, twisting together with the howls of monsters. You stand atop the crumbling lighthouse—encroaching corruption at your back, and before you, only the faintest glimmer of hope.
Side by side, you wait in the dark for the coming dawn.
